title: The Prawn Nebula from ESO's VST
caption: The Prawn Nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Glowing clouds of gas curl across this huge view of IC 4628, a stellar nursery nicknamed the Prawn Nebula for its shape. It was taken with the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, and may be the sharpest picture yet of this region.

Tucked into the clouds are clumps of hot, newborn stars. Their intense light energizes the surrounding gas and makes it glow, which is why stellar nurseries like this one shine in reds and pinks rather than sitting dark against the sky.

The VST is built for wide, sharp views of large patches of sky, and this one is enormous: the full image is many thousands of pixels across, so it rewards zooming in to find the knots, ridges and dark lanes of dust threaded through the nebula. Data from images by the astrophotographer Martin Pugh were also used to make it.

understand.summary: The VST's OmegaCAM camera recorded broad red and near-infrared bands plus a hydrogen-alpha filter, with extra narrowband data for oxygen and sulfur. Hydrogen-alpha appears in orange, oxygen in cyan and sulfur in yellow.
understand.eye: The nebula is far too faint for the eye; long exposures and narrow filters bring out the glow of its gas.
